districtText: Legislative District 34 | Congressional District 7 | King County

races.type: Federal Partisan Office • Vote for One
races.title: United States Representative, Congressional District No. 7
races.overview: The U.S. Representative for Washington's 7th Congressional District represents residents across Seattle, Vashon Island, Shoreline, and portions of Burien in the United States House of Representatives. Members of Congress are responsible for drafting, debating, and voting on federal legislation that shapes national policies and spending. They manage annual federal budget appropriations, oversee federal regulatory agencies, and serve on key legislative committees. Additionally, congressional offices provide vital constituent services, helping local residents navigate federal benefit programs like Social Security, Medicare, and veterans' assistance. Representatives also secure crucial federal grant funding for regional infrastructure, public transit, environmental restoration, and economic development projects across King County.

candidates.name: Pramila Jayapal
candidates.desc: Pramila Jayapal is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Congressional District 7, serving in office since 2017. As Chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus, she advocates for Medicare for All, climate action, consumer protection, and expanded workers' rights. Her legislative focus includes securing federal funding for Puget Sound environmental restoration, expanding affordable housing initiatives, and protecting reproductive healthcare rights nationwide. She emphasizes strong constituent advocacy, federal oversight, and progressive economic reforms to support working families across King County.
pros: Senior congressional leadership as Progressive Caucus Chair with high national legislative visibility.
Proven track record of securing federal grant dollars for Puget Sound transit and housing projects.
cons: National progressive focus sometimes draws criticism from moderate voters seeking bipartisan compromise.
Strong ideological platform faces political resistance in divided congressional chambers.

candidates.name: Nirav Sheth
candidates.desc: Nirav Sheth is a local small business owner and fiscal conservative campaigning to represent Congressional District 7. His platform focuses on reducing federal government spending, combating inflation, and supporting small business growth through tax incentives and regulatory relief. He prioritizes strengthening public safety, funding law enforcement agencies, and implementing stricter border security policies. Sheth advocates for balanced federal budgets and market-driven solutions to improve energy independence and economic opportunities throughout the Puget Sound region.
pros: Brings practical small business background focused on inflation control and tax relief.
Strong commitment to law enforcement funding and public safety resources.
cons: Faces steep electoral challenge in a heavily Democratic-leaning congressional district.
Limited previous experience holding elected public legislative office.

candidates.name: Gwen Kirkland
candidates.desc: Gwen Kirkland is a community organizer and small business advocate focused on grassroots neighborhood revitalization. Her platform centers on increasing federal grants for affordable housing development, expanded childcare subsidies, and public transit safety. She advocates for targeted financial support for women- and minority-owned small businesses navigating rising operational costs. Kirkland emphasizes community-led public safety initiatives, universal mental health access, and environmental sustainability for urban neighborhoods.
pros: Deep grassroots community connections with emphasis on small business advocacy.
Focuses on urban neighborhood childcare support and local mental health resources.
cons: Lacks prior federal legislative or congressional committee leadership experience.
Smaller campaign apparatus compared to established incumbent operations.

candidates.name: David W. Blomstrom
candidates.desc: David W. Blomstrom is an anti-establishment candidate and author running under the Fifth Republic party banner. He advocates for sweeping institutional reforms, increased political transparency, and strict campaign finance limitations. His platform challenges corporate lobbyist influence in federal lawmaking and calls for public auditing of governmental agencies. Blomstrom focuses on public education reform, wildlife conservation, and ending foreign corporate subsidies.
pros: Strong focus on government transparency, anti-corruption, and campaign finance reform.
Independent perspective unaligned with traditional corporate party platforms.
cons: Unconventional political party affiliation limits mainstream party backing.
Proposes radical institutional overhauls that may be difficult to enact legislatively.

races.type: State Partisan Office • Vote for One
races.title: Legislative District No. 34 – State Senator
races.overview: The Washington State Senator for Legislative District 34 represents West Seattle, White Center, Vashon Island, and Maury Island in the State Senate in Olympia. State Senators serve four-year terms and are responsible for crafting state statutes, establishing state tax policy, and enacting the biennium operating and capital budgets. They exercise legislative authority over public K-12 education, state transportation systems, environmental protection regulations, and public healthcare networks. The Senator works closely with executive state agencies to ensure regional infrastructure priorities, such as ferry service reliability and bridge maintenance, receive proper state funding. Legislative District 34 plays a key policy role in shaping progressive state laws regarding tenant protections, clean energy transitions, and tax equity.

candidates.name: Emily Alvarado
candidates.desc: Emily Alvarado is the incumbent State Senator for District 34 and a former Director of the Seattle Office of Housing. She focuses on expanding state investments in affordable housing construction, strengthening tenant protections, and funding public education. Her legislative priorities include enhancing ferry system reliability for Vashon Island residents, reducing carbon emissions, and protecting behavioral health services. Alvarado is endorsed by major labor organizations, environmental groups, and working-family advocacy coalitions across Washington State.
pros: Extensive executive housing policy expertise and active legislative record in Olympia.
Strong advocacy for Vashon Island ferry reliability and regional transit connections.
cons: Focus on state housing mandates faces scrutiny from neighborhood zoning traditionalists.
Progressive tax policy proposals draw opposition from fiscal conservative groups.

races.type: State Partisan Office • Vote for One
races.title: Legislative District No. 34 – Representative Position No. 1
races.overview: State Representatives serve two-year terms representing Legislative District 34 in the Washington State House of Representatives. As members of the legislature's lower chamber, Representatives introduce revenue bills, evaluate executive appointments, and write statewide statutory laws. They work directly on state fiscal policy, evaluating capital budget requests for local parks, schools, and community centers. Representatives advocate for district-specific transportation needs, including roadway safety, transit frequency, and maritime infrastructure. They also serve on specialized legislative committees covering labor relations, environmental health, civil rights, and state finance.

candidates.name: Brianna K. Thomas
candidates.desc: Brianna K. Thomas is the incumbent State Representative for District 34 Position 1 and a veteran labor advocate. She focuses on expanding collective bargaining rights, raising state minimum wage standards, and protecting low-income working families. Her legislative platform prioritizes equitable public school funding, reproductive healthcare protections, and environmental justice for frontline communities. Thomas actively works to secure state funding for local youth programs, affordable housing developments, and public safety infrastructure.
pros: Deep background in labor organizing, worker protections, and minimum wage advocacy.
Active champion for public school funding equity and local community services.
cons: Pro-worker regulatory emphasis faces opposition from business trade associations.
Focus on progressive state policy can face gridlock during tight budget cycles.

races.type: State Partisan Office • Vote for One
races.title: Legislative District No. 34 – Representative Position No. 2
races.overview: Representative Position 2 holds one of the two seats representing District 34 in the Washington State House of Representatives. Members of the House manage statewide statutory laws, state tax codes, and regulatory oversight across Washington. They collaborate with local municipal leaders to deliver state funding for critical municipal projects, environmental cleanup, and coastal protection. Representatives play a pivotal role in formulating state climate policy, renewable energy standards, and state transit grants. They also review legislative proposals affecting civil rights, judicial procedures, public safety, and higher education tuition funding.

candidates.name: Joe Fitzgibbon
candidates.desc: Joe Fitzgibbon serves as the House Majority Leader and incumbent Representative for District 34 Position 2. He is a primary author of Washington's landmark Climate Commitment Act and Clean Fuel Standard laws aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions. His legislative priorities include expanding regional light rail and transit networks, preserving salmon habitats, and modernizing state tax policy. Fitzgibbon works extensively on state budget negotiations, public education funding, and legislative strategy in Olympia.
pros: House Majority Leader with high legislative influence over state budget appropriations.
Statewide leader on landmark environmental legislation and clean energy policy.
cons: State clean energy policies face criticism over fuel tax and cost-of-living impacts.
Longtime incumbency draws calls for political turnover from outside reform groups.

races.type: County Nonpartisan Office • Vote for One
races.title: King County Assessor
races.overview: The King County Assessor is an independently elected, nonpartisan official responsible for establishing fair and equitable property valuations for all taxable real estate across King County. The Assessor's Department evaluates hundreds of thousands of residential, commercial, and industrial properties annually to form the county tax roll. While the Assessor does not set property tax rates or collect taxes, valuation determinations directly establish how property tax burdens are distributed among property owners. The office administers property tax exemption and deferral programs for senior citizens, low-income homeowners, disabled veterans, and non-profit organizations. Additionally, the Assessor provides public real estate data, manages valuation appeals processes, and ensures statutory compliance under Washington State tax laws.

candidates.name: Al Dams
candidates.desc: Al Dams is the Chief Deputy Assessor for King County with over 30 years of executive management experience within the Assessor's Department. He emphasizes operational stability, advanced computer-assisted mass appraisal technology, and strict adherence to statutory valuation rules. His platform focuses on expanding property tax relief outreach to senior citizens and disabled homeowners across all King County communities. Dams prioritizes staff training, transparent public reporting, and efficient property tax appeal processing.
pros: 30+ years of direct technical experience within the King County Assessor's Office.
Proven administrative track record with focus on senior homeowner tax relief.
cons: Associated with current department status-quo during period of high property valuations.
Less focused on sweeping structural changes to the assessment system.

candidates.name: Rob Foxcurran
candidates.desc: Rob Foxcurran is a Senior City Appraiser and professional real estate analyst endorsed by labor unions including PROTEC17. He advocates for modernizing property assessment algorithms to ensure accurate valuation adjustments for small business properties and residential homes. His platform emphasizes enhanced public transparency, accessible property valuation appeal resources, and equitable tax distribution. Foxcurran aims to streamline property assessment reviews and expand technical assistance for first-time home buyers.
pros: Technical appraiser background with strong endorsement from public sector labor unions.
Focuses on updating assessment algorithms for fair commercial vs. residential balance.
cons: Has not previously managed a county department of the Assessor's scale.
Proposed algorithm updates would require complex state regulatory approvals.

candidates.name: Christopher Roberts
candidates.desc: Christopher Roberts is a former Mayor of Shoreline who holds a Ph.D. in Political Science. He advocates for policy reforms that expand state property tax relief eligibility for low- and middle-income homeowners facing rising housing costs. His platform focuses on improving customer service accessibility, multi-lingual public outreach, and transparent valuation methodology. Roberts seeks to partner with local city councils to align property assessment practices with regional housing affordability goals.
pros: Proven mayoral leadership experience in municipal governance and public policy.
Emphasis on expanding property tax relief outreach to low-income homeowners.
cons: Lacks technical appraisal license background compared to deputy assessor candidates.
May face a learning curve regarding mass property appraisal software systems.

candidates.name: Dominique M. Scarimbolo
candidates.desc: Dominique M. Scarimbolo is a local small business owner and real estate advocate campaigning for property tax fairness. Her platform advocates for capping annual property tax assessment increases to protect fixed-income homeowners from tax displacement. She focuses on administrative transparency, simplifying valuation appeal procedures, and auditing assessment consistency across urban and rural King County precincts. Scarimbolo emphasizes consumer protection, fiscal accountability, and reducing government overhead costs.
pros: Strong advocate for capping property tax valuation spikes to protect homeowners.
Private sector business perspective focused on consumer advocacy.
cons: State constitution limits Assessor's unilateral power to cap tax valuations.
No prior public sector property appraisal department management experience.

races.type: County Nonpartisan Office • Vote for One
races.title: Metropolitan King County Council, District No. 8
races.overview: District 8 of the Metropolitan King County Council represents urban and unincorporated communities including West Seattle, White Center, Vashon Island, Maury Island, and downtown Seattle. Councilmembers exercise legislative authority over county government operations, approving a multi-billion dollar biennial budget for regional services. They govern Metro transit bus and water taxi systems, county public health clinics, regional parks, wastewater treatment, and sheriff public safety operations. The Council sets regional land-use policies, zoning regulations for unincorporated areas, and environmental conservation frameworks. Councilmembers also oversee county housing levies, behavioral health crisis centers, and regional homelessness response programs.

candidates.name: Teresa Mosqueda
candidates.desc: Teresa Mosqueda is the incumbent King County Councilmember for District 8 and former Seattle City Councilmember. She prioritizes regional investments in affordable housing, expanded Metro transit services, and crisis mental health facilities. Her legislative focus includes supporting working families through childcare subsidies, environmental health protections, and workforce development. Mosqueda is endorsed by labor organizations, housing advocates, and civic leaders across King County.
pros: Experienced municipal legislator with track record on workforce housing and healthcare.
Strong relationships with regional labor unions, housing providers, and civic leaders.
cons: Progressive spending priorities draw criticism from fiscal conservative groups.
Faced scrutiny over regional homelessness policy outcomes in urban centers.

candidates.name: Mia Jacobson
candidates.desc: Mia Jacobson is a neighborhood safety advocate and community volunteer focusing on urban revitalization. Her platform centers on increasing public safety resources, supporting local small businesses, and improving county budget transparency. She advocates for expanded behavioral health response teams, improved road infrastructure, and reliable ferry transit for Vashon Island. Jacobson emphasizes fiscal accountability, public safety collaboration, and constituent advocacy.
pros: Strong focus on neighborhood public safety, small business support, and budget transparency.
Grassroots community organizer with focus on Vashon Island ferry reliability.
cons: Lacks prior elected legislative office experience on a county level.
Smaller campaign fundraising footprint compared to the incumbent.

candidates.name: Nick Duda
candidates.desc: Nick Duda is a civic leader and business professional campaigning for public safety and fiscal discipline on the County Council. He advocates for expanding Sheriff's deputy staffing, modernizing emergency response systems, and auditing county spending programs. His platform focuses on streamlining commercial permitting processes to encourage local economic investment and job growth. Duda prioritizes practical infrastructure maintenance, park safety, and balanced county budget allocations.
pros: Prioritizes law enforcement staffing, public safety infrastructure, and spending audits.
Private sector business perspective focused on economic growth and job creation.
cons: Proposed police expansion faces opposition from progressive criminal justice reform groups.
First-time candidate navigating complex county legislative processes.

races.type: State Judicial Nonpartisan Office • Vote for One
races.title: State Supreme Court – Justice Position No. 1 (Unexpired Term)
races.overview: Justices of the Washington State Supreme Court sit on the state's highest judicial tribunal, reviewing major legal, constitutional, and statutory challenges. The Supreme Court has ultimate appellate jurisdiction over state legal matters, evaluating decisions issued by lower trial and appellate courts. Justices interpret the Washington State Constitution, review complex civil and criminal statutory appeals, and establish legal precedents binding on all state courts. The Court also exercises administrative oversight over the Washington legal system, governing attorney licensing, judicial conduct standards, and court rules of procedure. Supreme Court Justices serve nonpartisan, six-year staggered terms and must maintain judicial impartiality, constitutional fidelity, and commitment to equal access to justice.

candidates.name: Colleen Melody
candidates.desc: Colleen Melody is a Senior Assistant Attorney General and former Chief of the Civil Rights Division in the Washington Attorney General's Office. She brings extensive appellate litigation experience arguing constitutional and statutory cases before state and federal courts. Her platform emphasizes strict adherence to constitutional protections, judicial neutrality, and equal access to legal remedies for all residents. Melody is endorsed by legal scholars, retired judges, and statewide legal organizations.
pros: Extensive appellate trial background arguing high-level state constitutional cases.
Strong judicial endorsements and civil rights legal leadership background.
cons: Career spent primarily in executive state attorney office rather than as a trial court judge.
Public sector litigation background draws scrutiny from defense bar trade groups.

candidates.name: Laura Christensen Colberg
candidates.desc: Laura Christensen Colberg is an experienced trial and appellate attorney specializing in statutory interpretation and administrative law. She advocates for judicial restraint, maintaining clear legal precedents, and ensuring impartial legal analysis free from political influence. Her platform focuses on improving court efficiency, expanding pro bono legal resources, and protecting constitutional due process rights. Colberg emphasizes judicial independence and respectful civil discourse across the state court system.
pros: Focuses on judicial restraint, legal stability, and nonpartisan constitutional analysis.
Promotes expansion of pro bono legal access for underrepresented litigants.
cons: Lacks prior judicial bench service on state trial or appellate courts.
Lower public name recognition statewide compared to state AG candidates.

candidates.name: Scott Edwards
candidates.desc: Scott Edwards is a civil litigation attorney with decades of trial experience representing individuals, small businesses, and municipalities. He advocates for strict constitutional interpretation, protecting individual liberties, and maintaining predictable legal standards for state businesses. His platform emphasizes expanding public access to judicial records, modernizing court technology, and ensuring fair trial procedures. Edwards prioritizes judicial accountability, integrity, and timely court decisions.
pros: Decades of practical private civil trial litigation experience representing citizens and businesses.
Emphasis on court technology modernization and transparent judicial proceedings.
cons: Has not previously served on the judicial bench.
Civil litigation background may require broader orientation on complex criminal appellate procedure.
